tiers.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production environment background for TIER 2 of a THREE-tier cozy sushi restaurant game.
Reference roles: Image 1 is the humble tier-1 shop: mandatory art style, material palette, isometric viewing angle and recognizable entrance/window identity. Image 2 is a reference for the eventual larger bustling final restaurant; do not copy its UI or characters.
Primary request: Physically EXPAND the small starter shop into a noticeably wider, moderately larger established sushi bar. This is an architectural expansion, not merely a change of finish in the same footprint. About 35–45% more usable floor area than tier 1. Maintain believable human-sized furniture proportions and the same elevated orthographic isometric camera. All furniture must share one coherent scale. Preserve the familiar left sliding wooden entrance, small blossom-view window and two-wall open-front dollhouse construction, with extended wall bays and a wider floor platform.
Layout: a longer warm cedar L-shaped sushi counter, short return on RIGHT, FOUR evenly spaced matching sage-green cushioned wooden stools along the customer-facing long side. A genuinely spacious kitchen work aisle behind the counter. Expanded fitted kitchen along back wall: compact upright refrigerator, modest professional cooker and simple hood, rice pot, ivory tiled backsplash, sink, cabinetry, shelves with neatly stacked plain ceramic bowls and ingredient containers. Clear countertop for separate animated food and chef sprites. Enough working space for one chef; no second work bay yet. Wider customer aisle and a small clean welcome/service nook at the front-right. NO dining tables yet; reserve them for tier 3.
Atmosphere: fresh sage plaster, substantial timber framing, well-finished wooden plank floor with a modest wooden edge, restrained upper wall lattice and a few integrated warm lights. Thoughtfully furnished and welcoming, still below the grander final restaurant. Warm outlined pixel-like painted art exactly matching the reference, crisp readable game shapes and soft sunlight.
Composition: landscape 3:2 canvas, exactly 1536 x 1024, opaque pale warm cream background. Whole expanded building including floor platform fully visible, centered, safe margins on every side. No cropped corners, no roof. This should unmistakably read as the same restaurant after a first substantial expansion.
Layering constraints: Environment and fixed furniture ONLY. NO people, chefs, guests, animals, food plates, sushi, conveyor, glass sushi display cases, certificates, wall prints, lucky cats, potted plants, noren curtains or catalog paper lanterns. Keep their wall/floor/counter display areas clear for separate sprites. No UI, numbers, labels, readable text, logo or watermark. Do not include multiple panels.

tiers.layout: Larger full restaurant, five counter stools, two dining tables, expanded kitchen, waiting bench and tiled floor.
tiers.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production environment background for TIER 3, the FINAL cozy sushi restaurant.
Reference roles: Image 1 is tier 1, mandatory style/camera/architectural identity. Image 2 is newly expanded tier 2, intermediate development. Image 3 is the desired full-restaurant concept for layout richness and sense of activity; EXCLUDE its UI and all people.
Primary request: Expand the building AGAIN beyond tier 2 into a genuinely larger, fully established restaurant, inspired by the spacious final concept. The usable floor footprint should feel roughly twice tier 1, and clearly larger and deeper than tier 2. Show real added wall bays, floor space and functional areas; do not just upgrade finishes. Keep furniture believable at a coherent human-sized scale, the same elevated orthographic isometric viewing angle and cozy warm outlined pixel-like painted style. Keep the recognizable sliding wooden entrance on left wall and adjacent blossom-view window.
Layout: a substantial warm pale-hinoki L-shaped sushi counter in the middle-right with a short return on the right and FIVE matching premium sage-cushioned stools along its customer-facing edge. Broad clear counter for food sprites and optional purchased display equipment. Behind it, a professional open kitchen with TWO clearly usable preparation positions and a generous aisle: upright refrigerator, fitted range and silver hood, ivory tiled backsplash, rice pot, sink, cedar and dark pine cabinetry, organized utensil rails, shelves densely but neatly stacked with ordinary ceramic dishes and small ingredient containers. Leave room for separate chef and sous-chef sprites.
Additional dining area in the front-left: TWO small rectangular wooden tables, TWO wooden chairs per table, logically arranged with visible space to sit and a clear path from entrance to counter. Tables are empty of food. This added dining zone must unmistakably make the room feel larger than the counter-only tier 2. Front-right: small warm wooden waiting bench and low entrance railing, clear walkway, no register desk or money graphic.
Floor: attractive MATTE tiled floor, warm ivory alternating with muted slate-sage gray in a restrained checkerboard, thin beige grout, correct isometric square grid, framed by a dark wooden perimeter border. Floor visible through all areas, warm daylight/contact shadows, cozy not sterile.
Final-tier finish: cream plaster and muted sage panels, dark pine/cedar framing, fine traditional kumiko lattice details on upper wall sections, discreet amber architectural lighting, beautifully crafted warm counter fronts. Furnished, purposeful, prosperous, welcoming, with several distinct areas ready for diners. This should capture the reference concept's lively restaurant arrangement even before animated characters are added.
Composition: ONE full-room landscape 3:2 illustration exactly 1536 x 1024, opaque pale cream background. Whole larger building and every platform edge fully visible with safe margins. Two back walls, open front and no roof. Complete isometric cutaway, no cropped building or excessive empty outside margins.
Layering constraints: ENVIRONMENT AND FIXED FURNITURE ONLY. No people, chefs, customers, animals, sushi/food plates, food, conveyor belt, glass sushi display case, master certificate, golden cat, wall prints, potted plants, noren curtains or catalog paper lanterns: those are separate game layers. No UI, HUD, counters, text, numbers, logos, readable menus, labels or watermark. Keep interchangeable wall and floor decoration spots available. Do not draw multiple panels or a comparison.

layering: Characters, serving plates, conveyor, purchased display equipment and interchangeable decorations are excluded for separate animation layers. The larger layouts need new room anchors and foreground cutouts before runtime replacement.
